The Asian palm civet's long, stocky body is covered with coarse, shaggy hair that is usually greyish in colour.
It has a white mask across the forehead, a small white patch under each eye, a white spot on each side of the nostrils, and a narrow dark line between the eyes.

The marbled cat ( Pardofelis marmorata ) is a small wild cat native from the eastern Himalayas to Southeast Asia , where it inhabits forests up to an elevation of 2,500 m (8,200 ft).
In India, it is protected under Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 .
Marbled Cat needs a safe habitat with food, water and shelter.
The marbled cat is closely related to the Asian golden cat ( Catopuma temminckii ) and the bay cat ( C. badia ), all of which diverged from other felids about 9.4 million years ago.
The marbled cat is similar in size to a domestic cat , but has rounded ears and a very long tail that is as long as the cat's head and body.
The ground colour of its long fur varies from brownish-grey to ochreous brown above and greyish to buff below.
It is patterned with black stripes on the short and round head, on the neck and back.
On the tail, limbs and underbelly it has solid spots.
On the flanks it has irregular dark-edged blotches that fuse to dark areas and look like a 'marbled' pattern.
Its paws are webbed between the digits and are completely sheathed.
The Raffles' banded langur ( Presbytis femoralis ), also known as the banded leaf monkey or banded surili , is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae .

Scientists use the name Presbytis femoralis when they talk about the Banded Leaf Monkey.
Banded Leaf Monkey has special features that help it live in its habitat.

Surilis are rather small, slimly built primates .
Their fur at the top is brown, grey, black, or orange, and at the lower surface whitish or greyish, sometimes also orange, with some species having fur designs at the head or at the hips.

A few species have been observed in monogamous pairings (particularly the Mentawai langur ), although this might be a reaction to the decrease of their habitat.

Hose's Langur needs a safe habitat with food, water and shelter.
Hose's langur is commonly found in the northern and eastern regions of Malaysia as well as the northern part of Borneo.
They are most likely to be found in coastal regions with forests.
The Hose's langur's territory is small spanning no larger than 0.14 square miles.

The tufted ground squirrel or groove-toothed squirrel ( Rheithrosciurus macrotis ) is a species of rodent in the family Sciuridae .

It is the sole species in the genus Rheithrosciurus .
Confirmed elements of its diet include nuts, seeds and insects, for which it has been filmed foraging on the forest floor.

Its incisors have 7-10 distinctive longitudinal grooves.
Its skull is also distinctive, being longer and flatter than most squirrels.
The animal's dorsum is predominantly brown with a reddish tone, and it has unusually hairy ears with large red to dark brown tufts.
A longitudinal stripe of a white to buff to yellow colour, sometimes accompanied by a dark brown stripe, runs along the flank.
It may alternatively have a function in communicating with other squirrels or in courtship.

The northern treeshrew ( Tupaia belangeri ) is a treeshrew species native to Southeast Asia .

Northern Treeshrew has special features that help it live in its habitat.

This difference is larger than in other endotherms , and indicates that the circadian rhythms of body temperature and locomotor activity are synchronized.
Besides humans, the northern treeshrew is the only mammal known to willingly consume spicy food.
This is due to a genetic mutation rendering it much less sensitive to the effects of capsaicin.
Complete mitochondrial genome data support the hypothesis of a closer phylogenetic relationship of Tupaia to rabbits than to primates.

The paws are bare with sharp nails, and with a naked patch of skin above its long nose.
The animal has a head and body length of 13–21 cm and a tail length of 12–20 cm.
The common treeshrew usually has a white, pale stripe on each shoulder.
The two subspecies are T. g. longipes and T. g. salatana , with T. g. longipes being duller in color than T. g. salatana .
The large treeshrew ( Tupaia tana ) is a treeshrew species within the Tupaiidae .

Large treeshrews are most abundant in primary tropical rainforest , but are also found in swamp forest and secondary growth forest .
T. tana has many potential predators such as the marbled cat , leopard , and clouded leopard .
Large treeshrews contribute to the maintenance of their lowland rainforest ecosystem by dispersing seeds .
